name: Gurbaksh Chahal
milestone_by_age_26: Sold ClickAgents for a reported large acquisition price
starting_point: Born in Tarn Taran, Punjab, India; immigrated to San Jose, California at age 4 into a working-class Sikh family; father was a stock trader who lost his savings in a market crash.
current_position: CEO of VendorCloud and RedLotus; serial entrepreneur based in San Jose; net worth estimated in the hundreds of millions.

trajectory.title: Founded ClickAgents
trajectory.description: Dropped out of high school to launch ClickAgents, one of the first pay-per-click advertising networks, contracting a programmer in London to build the platform.

trajectory.title: Sold ClickAgents to ValueClick
trajectory.description: Sold ClickAgents for nearly $40 million, becoming a millionaire before turning 19.

trajectory.title: Co-founded BlueLithium
trajectory.description: Launched BlueLithium, a behavioral-targeting-focused internet advertising network that became the fifth-largest in the US.

trajectory.title: Sold BlueLithium to Yahoo
trajectory.description: Yahoo acquired BlueLithium for $300 million in cash, cementing Chahal's reputation as a serial ad-tech entrepreneur.

trajectory.title: Founded RadiumOne
trajectory.description: Launched RadiumOne, an ad network leveraging social data for targeted advertising.

trajectory.title: Founded Gravity4
trajectory.description: Started Gravity4, a marketing cloud platform, after departing RadiumOne amid legal controversy.

trajectory.title: Launched BNN Breaking
trajectory.description: Founded BNN Breaking, a global news platform, expanding his entrepreneurial portfolio beyond ad-tech.

trajectory.title: CEO of VendorCloud and RedLotus
trajectory.description: Leading VendorCloud and RedLotus while continuing to build new ventures in AI and enterprise technology.

name: John Zimmer
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Zimride, predecessor to Lyft
starting_point: Born in Greenwich, Connecticut; father was Larry Zimmer; studied at Cornell University's School of Hotel Administration, inspired by hospitality from an early job at a Hyatt hotel.
current_position: Co-founder and Vice Chair of Lyft's board of directors; stepped down as President in June 2023; net worth estimated in the hundreds of millions.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Cornell University
trajectory.description: Graduated from Cornell's School of Hotel Administration and joined Lehman Brothers as a real estate finance analyst in New York.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Zimride
trajectory.description: Co-founded Zimride with Logan Green, a college carpooling platform, while still working at Lehman Brothers; launched first at Cornell where 20% of students signed up in six months.

trajectory.title: Left Lehman Brothers for Zimride full-time
trajectory.description: Quit Lehman Brothers three months before its bankruptcy and moved to Silicon Valley with Green to work on Zimride full-time.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Lyft
trajectory.description: Spun out Lyft from Zimride as a peer-to-peer, on-demand ride-sharing app, raising $7.5 million in funding.

trajectory.title: Sold Zimride to Enterprise Holdings
trajectory.description: Sold the original Zimride carpooling service to Enterprise Holdings to focus entirely on Lyft.

trajectory.title: Named to Fortune 40 Under 40
trajectory.description: Named to Fortune's 40 Under 40 list for the second time, recognized as one of the most influential young people in business.

trajectory.title: Lyft IPO on Nasdaq
trajectory.description: Lyft listed its shares on Nasdaq on March 29, 2019, with over 30 million riders and 1.9 million drivers in 2018.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as Lyft President
trajectory.description: Announced he would step down as Lyft president in June 2023, transitioning to Vice Chair of the board of directors.

name: Logan Green
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Zimride
starting_point: Born in Los Angeles, California; grew up in Culver City; graduated from UC Santa Barbara with a BA in Business Economics; fascinated by transportation from childhood experiences stuck in traffic.
current_position: Venture Partner at Autotech Ventures; former CEO and Chairman of Lyft; stepped down as Lyft CEO in April 2023 and as board chair in August 2025.

trajectory.title: Graduated from UCSB
trajectory.description: Graduated from UC Santa Barbara with a degree in Business Economics; served as the youngest director for the Santa Barbara Metropolitan Transit District.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Zimride
trajectory.description: Founded Zimride with John Zimmer, a ride-sharing platform for college campuses, inspired by carpooling practices he observed while studying in Zimbabwe.

trajectory.title: Moved to Palo Alto
trajectory.description: Moved to a two-bedroom apartment in Palo Alto with Zimmer to work on Zimride full-time; neither drew a salary for the first three years.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Lyft
trajectory.description: Spun out Lyft from Zimride as a mobile, peer-to-peer ride-hailing service, pivoting from the web-based carpooling model.

trajectory.title: Joined eBay board
trajectory.description: Appointed to the board of directors of eBay, Inc., expanding his governance experience beyond Lyft.

trajectory.title: Led Lyft through IPO
trajectory.description: Lyft went public on Nasdaq under his leadership as CEO, becoming the first ride-hailing company to IPO.

trajectory.title: Stepped down as Lyft CEO
trajectory.description: Stepped down as CEO of Lyft in April 2023, transitioning to Chairman of the board.

trajectory.title: Joined Autotech Ventures
trajectory.description: Became a Venture Partner at Autotech Ventures, a transportation-focused venture capital firm, in July 2024.

name: Vijay Shekhar Sharma
milestone_by_age_26: Founded One97 Communications
starting_point: Born in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh, India to a schoolteacher father and homemaker mother; studied in Hindi medium; enrolled in engineering college at age 15 and graduated at 19 from Delhi College of Engineering.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Paytm (One97 Communications); net worth approximately $1.2 billion; based in Noida, India.

trajectory.title: Founded indiasite.net
trajectory.description: Started the website indiasite.net while in college and sold it two years later for approximately $1 million.

trajectory.title: Founded One97 Communications
trajectory.description: Launched One97 Communications, offering mobile content including news, cricket scores, ringtones, and exam results; initially earning only Rs 10,000 per month.

trajectory.title: Launched Paytm
trajectory.description: Launched Paytm as a digital payments and financial services brand under One97 Communications, investing $2 million of his own money.

trajectory.title: Paytm surged during demonetization
trajectory.description: India's demonetization drive rendered 80% of physical currency worthless overnight, causing massive adoption of Paytm's digital wallet.

trajectory.title: Named India's youngest billionaire
trajectory.description: Forbes named him India's youngest billionaire with a net worth of $1.7 billion; launched Paytm Mall e-commerce branch.

trajectory.title: Warren Buffett invested in Paytm
trajectory.description: Warren Buffett made a $300 million investment in Paytm, a notable endorsement from the legendary investor.

trajectory.title: Paytm IPO
trajectory.description: Paytm went public raising $2.5 billion at a valuation of $19 billion, India's largest IPO at the time.

trajectory.title: Stepped down from Paytm Payments Bank
trajectory.description: Stepped down as part-time non-executive chairman of Paytm Payments Bank following regulatory challenges with the Reserve Bank of India.

name: Binny Bansal
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Flipkart
starting_point: Born in Chandigarh, India; father was a chief manager at a bank and mother worked in the government sector; graduated from IIT Delhi with a degree in computer science and engineering.
current_position: Entrepreneur-investor and mentor; co-founder of xto10x Technologies; anchor investor in 021 Capital; net worth estimated at $1.4 billion as of 2024.

trajectory.title: Graduated from IIT Delhi
trajectory.description: Graduated from IIT Delhi with a computer science engineering degree; worked at Sarnoff Corporation as a software engineer.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Flipkart
trajectory.description: Co-founded Flipkart with Sachin Bansal after nine months at Amazon, starting as an online bookstore from a two-bedroom flat in Bengaluru with Rs 400,000 in capital.

trajectory.title: Flipkart raised $1 billion
trajectory.description: Flipkart raised $1 billion at a $7 billion valuation, entering the global stage as one of the most valuable startups.

trajectory.title: Promoted to CEO of Flipkart
trajectory.description: Promoted from COO to CEO of Flipkart in January 2016, focusing on improving efficiency and cutting costs.

trajectory.title: Promoted to Group CEO
trajectory.description: Promoted to Group CEO of Flipkart in January 2017.

trajectory.title: Walmart acquired majority stake in Flipkart
trajectory.description: Steered Flipkart to close the largest M&A deal in e-commerce when Walmart acquired a majority stake for $16 billion.

trajectory.title: Resigned from Flipkart
trajectory.description: Resigned as Group CEO in November 2018 following allegations of personal misconduct.

trajectory.title: Co-founded xto10x Technologies
trajectory.description: Co-founded xto10x Technologies, offering technology tools and consultancy services to help growth-stage startups scale.

name: Adam D'Angelo
milestone_by_age_26: Became Chief Technology Officer of Facebook in 2006 at age 22, then co-founded Quora in June 2009 at age 24, both before age 26.
starting_point: Born in Redding, Connecticut; attended Phillips Exeter Academy where he developed Synapse Media Player with Mark Zuckerberg; graduated from Caltech with a BS in computer science.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Quora; board member of OpenAI and Asana; net worth estimated in the hundreds of millions.

trajectory.title: Joined Facebook
trajectory.description: Joined Facebook shortly after its launch while still attending Caltech, working on early engineering.

trajectory.title: Became Facebook CTO
trajectory.description: Served as Chief Technology Officer of Facebook from November 2006 to June 2008, overseeing engineering during the platform's explosive growth.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Quora
trajectory.description: Co-founded Quora with former Facebook engineer Charlie Cheever in June 2009, building a question-and-answer platform.

trajectory.title: Invested $20M in Quora Series B
trajectory.description: Personally invested $20 million in Quora as part of the company's $50 million Series B round of financing.

trajectory.title: Quora reached 100M monthly visitors
trajectory.description: Quora reached 100 million monthly visitors and launched Quora en Espanol, expanding internationally.

trajectory.title: Joined OpenAI board
trajectory.description: Appointed as a director on the OpenAI board, bringing deep technical expertise to the AI lab's governance.

trajectory.title: Launched Poe AI platform
trajectory.description: Quora launched Poe, an AI-powered platform for interacting with multiple language models, pivoting the company toward AI.

name: Max Rafael Levchin
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Fieldlink (later Confinity, then PayPal) with Peter Thiel in 1998 at age 23, serving as CTO and building the anti-fraud systems including one of the first commercial CAPTCHAs; PayPal went public in February 2002 at age 26 and was acquired by eBay later that year.
starting_point: Born in Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR to a Ukrainian-Jewish family of physicists; immigrated to Chicago in 1991 as a refugee with $700; graduated from University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign with a BS in computer science in 1997.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Affirm Holdings; net worth approximately $2 billion; based in San Francisco.

trajectory.title: Founded first startups at UIUC
trajectory.description: Founded NetMeridian Software and SponsorNet New Media with fellow University of Illinois students while still in college.

trajectory.title: Co-founded PayPal (Confinity)
trajectory.description: Co-founded Fieldlink, later renamed Confinity and then PayPal, with Peter Thiel; built anti-fraud systems including the Gausebeck-Levchin test, one of the first commercial CAPTCHAs.

trajectory.title: PayPal IPO and eBay acquisition
trajectory.description: PayPal went public in February 2002 and was acquired by eBay later that year; Levchin served as CTO throughout.

trajectory.title: Founded Slide
trajectory.description: Founded Slide, a social media app company that became one of the most popular Facebook app developers.

trajectory.title: Sold Slide to Google
trajectory.description: Google acquired Slide for approximately $182 million.

trajectory.title: Founded Affirm
trajectory.description: Founded Affirm, a buy-now-pay-later online lending company, applying fintech expertise from PayPal to consumer credit.

trajectory.title: Affirm IPO
trajectory.description: Affirm went public on Nasdaq in January 2021, with Levchin as CEO; the company was valued at over $12 billion at IPO.

name: Patrick Collison
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Stripe (originally /dev/payments), a payment infrastructure company, with his brother John in 2010 at age 22, which grew into a company valued at tens of billions of dollars; previously co-founded and sold Auctomatic for $5 million in 2008 at age 19.
starting_point: Born in Limerick, Ireland to microbiologist mother Lily and electronic engineer father Denis; grew up in Dromineer, County Tipperary; began programming at age 10; won the Young Scientist Exhibition at 16; attended MIT before dropping out.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Stripe; net worth estimated at $17.5 billion as of 2026; co-founder of Arc Institute.

trajectory.title: Won Young Scientist Exhibition
trajectory.description: Won the 41st Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition in Ireland for creating Croma, a LISP-type programming language.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Shuppa/Auctomatic
trajectory.description: Co-founded Shuppa with brother John in Limerick; moved to California after Y Combinator showed interest; merged with Oxford graduates to form Auctomatic.

trajectory.title: Sold Auctomatic for $5M
trajectory.description: Auctomatic was acquired for $5 million in March 2008, when Patrick was 19.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Stripe
trajectory.description: Co-founded Stripe (originally /dev/payments) with brother John, building programmable financial infrastructure for the internet.

trajectory.title: Founded Fast Grants
trajectory.description: Founded Fast Grants with economist Tyler Cowen to fund COVID-19-related science, distributing grants rapidly to researchers.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Arc Institute
trajectory.description: Co-founded Arc Institute, a nonprofit biomedical research organization, with bioscientists Silvana Konermann and Patrick Hsu.

trajectory.title: Stripe valued at $70B
trajectory.description: Stripe's valuation reached approximately $70 billion after a share transaction, making the Collison brothers among the wealthiest tech founders globally.

name: John Collison
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Stripe in 2010 at age 20 with his brother Patrick; Stripe received backing from Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, Max Levchin, and Sequoia Capital, and Collison became the world's youngest self-made billionaire by 2016 at age 25-26.
starting_point: Born in Limerick, Ireland to microbiologist mother Lily and electronic engineer father Denis; grew up in Dromineer, County Tipperary; attended Harvard University before dropping out to start Stripe.
current_position: Co-founder and President of Stripe; net worth estimated at $9.3 billion as of 2026 per Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Shuppa
trajectory.description: Co-founded Shuppa with brother Patrick in Limerick, which later merged with two Oxford graduates to become Auctomatic, funded by Y Combinator.

trajectory.title: Auctomatic acquired for $5M
trajectory.description: Auctomatic was acquired for $5 million in March 2008 when Collison was 17, before he had even started at Harvard.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Stripe
trajectory.description: Co-founded Stripe with brother Patrick, building payment infrastructure for the internet; received backing from Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, and Sequoia Capital.

trajectory.title: Became youngest self-made billionaire
trajectory.description: Became the world's youngest self-made billionaire after an investment from CapitalG and General Catalyst valued Stripe at $9.2 billion.

trajectory.title: Stripe continued rapid growth
trajectory.description: Stripe's valuation reached $36 billion, solidifying its position as one of the most valuable private tech companies.

trajectory.title: Stripe valued at $70B
trajectory.description: Stripe's valuation reached approximately $70 billion after a share transaction, with the Collison brothers each worth over $7 billion.

name: Aaron Swartz
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored the RSS 1.0 specification at age 14 in 2000, became co-owner of Reddit through the Infogami merger in 2005 at age 19, and Reddit was acquired by Conde Nast in 2006 for approximately $5 million at age 20, all well before age 26.
starting_point: Born in Highland Park, Illinois to a Jewish family; showed early programming talent; attended Stanford University briefly before dropping out to pursue technology and activism.
current_position: Died on January 11, 2013 at age 26 in New York City by suicide; final role: research fellow at Harvard University's Safra Research Lab and founder of Demand Progress.

trajectory.title: Co-authored RSS 1.0
trajectory.description: Co-authored the RSS 1.0 specification, a web feed format for syndicating content, at age 14.

trajectory.title: Worked on Creative Commons
trajectory.description: Helped develop the technical architecture for Creative Commons, an organization dedicated to creating flexible copyright licenses.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Reddit via Infogami merger
trajectory.description: His startup Infogami merged with Reddit, making him a co-owner; he contributed to Reddit's early development.

trajectory.title: Reddit acquired by Conde Nast
trajectory.description: Reddit was acquired by Conde Nast Publications for approximately $5 million; Swartz became a millionaire from the sale.

trajectory.title: Left Reddit
trajectory.description: Left Reddit and became increasingly involved in activism and progressive political organizing.

trajectory.title: Founded Demand Progress
trajectory.description: Founded the online group Demand Progress, known for its campaign against the Stop Online Piracy Act (SOPA).

trajectory.title: Arrested for JSTOR downloading
trajectory.description: Arrested by MIT campus police for systematically downloading academic journal articles from JSTOR, leading to a federal indictment.

trajectory.title: Died in New York City
trajectory.description: Died by suicide on January 11, 2013, while facing federal charges that could have resulted in decades of imprisonment.

name: Justin Frankel
milestone_by_age_26: Created and publicly released Winamp, the dominant MP3 player software, at age 19 in 1997; by 1998 it had over 15 million downloads and he founded Nullsoft to distribute it.
starting_point: Born in 1978 and grew up in Sedona, Arizona; showed early aptitude for computers, running the student computer network at Verde Valley School; attended University of Utah briefly before dropping out.
current_position: Founder of Cockos Incorporated, creating REAPER digital audio workstation and other music production software; based in the United States.

trajectory.title: Released Winamp
trajectory.description: Released the first version of Winamp, a media player for MP3 files, after dropping out of the University of Utah; founded Nullsoft to distribute it.

trajectory.title: Winamp reached 15M downloads
trajectory.description: Winamp surpassed 15 million downloads, earning Frankel tens of thousands of dollars per month from $10 voluntary donations.

trajectory.title: AOL acquired Nullsoft
trajectory.description: AOL acquired Nullsoft and Spinner.com in a combined deal worth approximately $400 million; Frankel became an AOL employee.

trajectory.title: Released Gnutella
trajectory.description: Created and released Gnutella, a decentralized peer-to-peer file-sharing network, without AOL's approval; AOL pulled the program but it spread widely.

trajectory.title: Left AOL
trajectory.description: Departed AOL after tensions over Gnutella and other unauthorized projects, ending his tenure at the company.

trajectory.title: Founded Cockos Incorporated
trajectory.description: Founded Cockos, creating the REAPER digital audio workstation, NINJAM collaborative music tool, and other music production software.

trajectory.title: Continued REAPER development
trajectory.description: Continued developing REAPER, which became one of the most respected digital audio workstations among professional musicians and producers.

name: Evan You
milestone_by_age_26: Released Vue.js, a lightweight JavaScript frontend framework, publicly on GitHub and Hacker News in February 2014 at age 26, attracting immediate community adoption and growing into one of the top three frontend frameworks globally.
starting_point: Born in Wuxi, Jiangsu, China in 1989; attended Fudan University Affiliated High School; earned a BA in Art History from Colgate University and an MFA in Design & Technology from Parsons School of Design.
current_position: Founder and CEO of VoidZero (acquired by Cloudflare in 2026); creator of Vue.js and Vite; based in Singapore.

trajectory.title: Joined Google Creative Lab
trajectory.description: Joined Google Creative Lab as a creative technologist, working on UI/UX prototypes including Google Glass and iOS search app projects.

trajectory.title: Released Vue.js
trajectory.description: Released Vue.js publicly on GitHub and Hacker News in February 2014 as a personal side project, attracting immediate community adoption.

trajectory.title: Became full-time independent OSS developer
trajectory.description: Left Meteor Development Group to maintain Vue.js full-time, becoming one of the first developers to sustain an open-source project through Patreon crowdfunding.

trajectory.title: Released Vite
trajectory.description: Released Vite, a frontend build tool that became the dominant build-tool foundation for modern JavaScript application development.

trajectory.title: Founded VoidZero
trajectory.description: Founded VoidZero, a company building the next-generation JavaScript and TypeScript toolchain, consolidating development of Vite and related tools.

trajectory.title: VoidZero acquired by Cloudflare
trajectory.description: VoidZero was acquired by Cloudflare; You joined Cloudflare to lead open source development of Vite, Vitest, Rolldown, and Oxc.

name: Dan Abramov
milestone_by_age_26: Released Redux, a JavaScript state management library, in June 2015 at age 22, which quickly became the dominant state management solution in the React ecosystem with billions of npm downloads.
starting_point: Born in Russia; grew up in a humble background; learned programming from bootleg VBA books as a teenager; landed first software developer job in 2010 at age 17.
current_position: Software engineer on the React team at Meta (Facebook); based in London; co-author of Redux and Create React App.

trajectory.title: First software developer job
trajectory.description: Landed first software development job in Russia after struggling with higher education, marking the beginning of his career.

trajectory.title: Released Redux
trajectory.description: Created and released Redux, a JavaScript state management library, to demonstrate time-travel debugging for a conference talk; it became the dominant state management solution in React.

trajectory.title: Joined Facebook React team
trajectory.description: Joined Facebook (Meta) as a software engineer working on the React team, contributing to the framework's development and ecosystem.

trajectory.title: Co-authored Create React App
trajectory.description: Co-authored Create React App, a tool that became the standard way to bootstrap React applications, further shaping the ecosystem.

trajectory.title: Redux ecosystem maturity
trajectory.description: Redux reached billions of npm downloads and became a foundational part of the React ecosystem, with Abramov as a leading voice in the community.

trajectory.title: Published My Decade in Review
trajectory.description: Published a widely-read personal retrospective covering his journey from a 17-year-old in Russia to a leading figure in the JavaScript world.

name: Bram Cohen
milestone_by_age_26: Released the first BitTorrent client and protocol implementation on July 2, 2001 at age 25, creating what would become one of the most widely used peer-to-peer file-sharing protocols, accounting for 43-70% of all internet traffic by 2009.
starting_point: Born on October 12, 1975 on the Upper West Side of Manhattan; son of a teacher and computer scientist; learned BASIC at age 5 on a Timex Sinclair; attended Stuyvesant High School and SUNY Buffalo before dropping out.
current_position: Co-founder, Chairman, and CEO of Chia Network; inventor of BitTorrent; based in the San Francisco Bay Area.

trajectory.title: Graduated from Stuyvesant High School
trajectory.description: Graduated from Stuyvesant High School in New York City after passing the AIME and qualifying for the USAMO; attended SUNY Buffalo.

trajectory.title: Worked at MojoNation
trajectory.description: Worked at MojoNation, an ambitious peer-to-peer project, throughout the late 1990s dot-com era, gaining experience in distributed systems.

trajectory.title: Released BitTorrent
trajectory.description: Released the first BitTorrent client and protocol on July 2, 2001, unveiling it at the first CodeCon conference he co-created.

trajectory.title: Founded BitTorrent, Inc.
trajectory.description: Founded BitTorrent, Inc. to commercialize the protocol, serving as initial CEO and later in engineering and board roles.

trajectory.title: BitTorrent dominated internet traffic
trajectory.description: BitTorrent accounted for 43-70% of all internet traffic, making it one of the most impactful protocols ever created.

trajectory.title: Founded Chia Network
trajectory.description: Left BitTorrent in August 2017 to found Chia Network, a cryptocurrency company implementing proof-of-space-time consensus.

trajectory.title: Became Chia CEO
trajectory.description: Became CEO of Chia Network in June 2019, leading the company's development of an eco-friendly blockchain.

name: Guillermo Rauch
milestone_by_age_26: Created and publicly released Socket.IO in 2010 at approximately age 23-24, an influential open-source real-time communication library that became one of the most widely used web frameworks, powering products at Microsoft Office, Yammer, Zendesk, and the first Coinbase trading platform. He also co-founded LearnBoost in 2010, one of the earliest production adopters of Node.js.
starting_point: Born in Lanus, Buenos Aires, Argentina; self-taught engineer who never finished high school; began coding at age 10-13 building websites for international clients; relocated to San Francisco at age 18.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Vercel, valued at approximately $9.3 billion; creator of Socket.IO and co-creator of Next.js; prolific angel investor with over 700 investments.

trajectory.title: Joined MooTools core team
trajectory.description: Joined the MooTools JavaScript framework core team, becoming recognized in the open-source JavaScript community as a teenager.

trajectory.title: First full-time frontend engineer in SF
trajectory.description: Got first full-time job as a frontend engineer at age 18 and relocated to San Francisco, California.

trajectory.title: Created Socket.IO
trajectory.description: Created Socket.IO, a real-time event communication library that became the de facto WebSocket standard for Node.js, powering millions of apps.

trajectory.title: Created Mongoose
trajectory.description: Created Mongoose, the most popular MongoDB object modeling library for Node.js.

trajectory.title: Cloudup acquired by Automattic
trajectory.description: Co-founded Cloudup, a file-sharing platform, which was acquired by Automattic (WordPress); joined as CTO working on media and editing technology.

trajectory.title: Founded Vercel (formerly Zeit)
trajectory.description: Founded Vercel to build cloud infrastructure and developer tooling for the web, focusing on developer experience.

trajectory.title: Co-created Next.js
trajectory.description: Co-created Next.js, which became the world's most popular React framework, powering sites for Washington Post, Porsche, and Nintendo.

name: Russel Simmons
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Yelp in October 2004 at approximately age 25-26 with Jeremy Stoppelman, serving as CTO from July 2004 to June 2010. Yelp became a major public internet company (IPO 2012) and one of the leading user-generated review platforms. Prior to Yelp, Simmons was a co-founder and Lead Software Architect at PayPal.
starting_point: Graduated from University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 1998 with a BS in Computer Science; also graduated from the Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy.
current_position: Founder and Chief of Learnirvana, Inc., focused on education technology and language learning; based in the San Francisco Bay Area.

trajectory.title: Graduated from UIUC
trajectory.description: Graduated from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign with a BS in Computer Science.

trajectory.title: Joined PayPal as Lead Software Architect
trajectory.description: Left graduate school at Illinois to join PayPal, co-founded by fellow UIUC alumnus Max Levchin; helped design the web-based payment system from scratch.

trajectory.title: Left PayPal after eBay acquisition
trajectory.description: Departed PayPal after its acquisition by eBay, joining the PayPal Mafia network of serial entrepreneurs.

trajectory.title: Co-founded Yelp
trajectory.description: Co-founded Yelp with Jeremy Stoppelman in a Max Levchin incubator, serving as CTO; the site became a leading user-generated review platform.

trajectory.title: Left Yelp
trajectory.description: Left Yelp in June 2010 after six years as CTO, transitioning to an advisor role and taking time off to travel.

trajectory.title: Founded Learnirvana
trajectory.description: Founded Learnirvana, focusing on new approaches to education including video-based foreign language learning.

trajectory.title: Yelp IPO
trajectory.description: Yelp went public on the NYSE in March 2012, reaching a market capitalization of over $1 billion on its first day of trading.

name: Felix Kjellberg (PewDiePie)
milestone_by_age_26: Became YouTube's most-subscribed individual creator
starting_point: Born on October 24, 1989 in Gothenburg, Sweden; parents were both successful chief executives; attended Chalmers University of Technology for industrial economics before dropping out to pursue YouTube.
current_position: Semi-retired YouTuber living in Japan with his wife Marzia; over 100 million subscribers; net worth estimated at $40-50 million.

trajectory.title: Registered PewDiePie YouTube channel
trajectory.description: Registered his YouTube channel PewDiePie, primarily posting Let's Play videos of horror and action video games from his bedroom.

trajectory.title: Rapid channel growth
trajectory.description: His channel became one of the fastest-growing on YouTube, surpassing 3 million subscribers by the end of the year.

trajectory.title: Became most-subscribed on YouTube
trajectory.description: Became the most-subscribed channel on YouTube on August 15, 2013, reaching over 12 million subscribers.

trajectory.title: Most-viewed channel on YouTube
trajectory.description: From December 29, 2014, his channel was also the most-viewed on the platform, cementing his status as YouTube's biggest star.

trajectory.title: Named highest-earning YouTuber

name: Emma Chamberlain

name: Virat Kohli
milestone_by_age_26: Became India's Test captain after a major international career
starting_point: Born on November 5, 1988 in New Delhi into a Punjabi Hindu family; father was a criminal lawyer, mother a homemaker; showed early affinity for cricket at age 3; trained at West Delhi Cricket Academy from 1998.

trajectory.title: Released All Eyez on Me

trajectory.title: Died in Las Vegas
